title: Comfort in Trials - Episode 4: Weeping May Endure for a Night

parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, a soft smile in the voice, speaking slowly
parts.text: Good evening, friend. <short pause> You're listening to Comfort in Trials, and I'm your host, David Lee. <short pause> Episode four is called Weeping May Endure for a Night. <short pause> Tonight, I'd like to ask you something... <short pause> what do we do, when sorrow fills the dark hours?

The psalmist knew something about weeping that lasts through the night. <short pause> He had faced death... stood at the edge of the grave... and cried out to God from a place of deep distress. <short pause> But he also knew something about morning. <short pause> Listen to what he says, in Psalm thirty, verse five.
For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning. <long pause>

This is not a denial of pain. <short pause> The psalmist doesn't say weeping is imaginary, or that sorrow is forbidden. <short pause> He says it endures for a night... which means it's real, it takes time, and it can feel very long.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: A night of weeping is still a night. <short pause> The hours pass slowly when you're hurting. <short pause> You watch the darkness... you feel the weight... and you wonder if morning will ever come.
But here's the promise tucked into this verse. <short pause> Night has a limit. <short pause> Weeping may endure... but it does not endure forever. <short pause> Joy comes in the morning.

The word for joy here is a word about singing... a shout of gladness. <short pause> It's the kind of joy that breaks through... not because you worked it up, or pretended hard enough... but because God brings it.

Morning in Scripture often points to new mercy... to the faithfulness of God, showing up again. <short pause> The prophet Jeremiah understood this. <short pause> He wrote the book of Lamentations in the midst of devastating loss, when Jerusalem had fallen, and everything seemed broken. <short pause> And yet, right in the middle of that book of sorrow... he stops to remember something.

It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness. <short pause> Lamentations, chapter three, verses twenty-two and twenty-three. <long pause>
New every morning. <short pause> Not once in a while. Not when we've earned it. <short pause> Every single morning.

This is what holds you, when the night feels endless. <short pause> Not your own strength. Not your ability to stay positive. <short pause> But the steady, unchanging faithfulness of God. <short pause> He does not grow weary. <short pause> He does not forget you in the dark.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: The sunrise is not just a feature of creation. <short pause> It's a daily picture of God's character. <short pause> Every morning says... I am still here. <short pause> I am still faithful. <short pause> My mercies have not run out.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: You may be lying here tonight, carrying something heavy. <short pause> Maybe it's grief that won't let go. Or fear about tomorrow. Or a hurt that hasn't healed. <exhales> Maybe you've been in this same struggle for so long, that you've started to wonder if morning will ever really come for you.

The promise is not that your circumstances will change overnight. <short pause> The promise is that God's mercies will meet you when morning comes. <short pause> New every morning. <short pause> Not the same old worn-out hope... but fresh mercy, for this new day.

Weeping may endure for a night... but it is not the end of the story. <short pause> God has set a rhythm into creation itself. <short pause> Darkness, then light. Night, then morning. Sorrow, then joy. <short pause> You can trust that rhythm... because you can trust the One who made it.

His anger, the verse says, endures but a moment. <short pause> His favor lasts a lifetime. <short pause> Even when discipline, or consequence, brings pain... it is brief, compared to the long, faithful love of God that never lets you go.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: So tonight, if you are weeping... let yourself weep. <short pause> God has made room for sorrow. <short pause> But also hold on to this... the night will not last forever. <short pause> When morning comes, mercy will be waiting. <short pause> And one day, in the full morning of eternity, weeping will be gone completely... and joy will fill everything.

Let's pray. <short pause> Father, thank you that your mercies are new every morning... and that your faithfulness is great. <short pause> Hold us through this night... and meet us with fresh mercy when morning comes.
